content:
Today is Election Day in Webb County. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, and voters who are in line by 7 p.m. can still cast a ballot. Texas requires an approved form of photo identification to vote in person, and voters should confirm their polling place before heading out through the Texas Secretary of State's voter portal at VoteTexas.gov.

Early voting closed Friday, October 30, with 46,332 ballots cast — 45,483 in person and 849 by mail — according to KGNS, citing the Webb County Elections Administration. The final day alone produced 6,130 votes, the highest single-day turnout of the two-week early voting period.

The mayor's race is citywide, with five candidates on the ballot: incumbent Mayor Victor D. Treviño, City Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa, JD Gonzalez, Jorge A. Garza and Alfonso “Poncho” Casso. Voters will also decide City Council Districts 1, 2, 3 and 6, and Municipal Court Judge, Place 1.

City voters also face Proposition 1, a non-binding advisory question asking whether the City of Laredo should support efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in the Laredo–Webb County community and encourage Webb County to evaluate available governmental options under Texas law. The measure, ordered by Resolution 2026-R-221, does not by itself authorize any tax, debt, expenditure, contract or construction.

Beyond City Hall, the same ballot carries the U.S. Senate race between Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, and the TX-28 House contest. Mail-in ballots must reach the county early voting clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, or by 5 p.m. Wednesday, November 4, if postmarked by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

One date remains after today: District 8 voters get their own special election on Saturday, December 5, with early voting November 23 through December 1.
